function: Joint BS transmit beamforming (communication and sensing beams) and STAR-RIS transmitting/reflecting phase-shift control by deep RL, minimizing average transmit power under delay and sensing-SNR constraints (p. 1-2, 5-6).
system: Near-field ISAC: multi-antenna ground BS (M not given), L single-antenna ground users, Z aerial targets, STAR-RIS up to about 1000 elements; B=10 MHz; carrier not stated (p. 4, 11-12).
method: Deep reinforcement learning: Lyapunov-based DDPG (actor-critic) and robust policy-based DRL with convex approximation (CMDP, CVX policy update), trained online by episodes (p. 7-10).
data_channel: Simulated: far-field direct and GBS-to-STAR-RIS links, near-field spherical-wave STAR-RIS-to-user links, random traffic arrivals in [0, 5] Mbit/s; no standardized model or dataset named (p. 5-6, 11).
test_conditions: No separate test phase stated: results are convergence curves over episodes and sweeps over STAR-RIS elements, delay threshold 0.5-5 ms, sensing threshold 10-35 dB, aerial users (p. 11-13).
baselines: Non-learned: random beamforming and STAR-RIS phase shifts. Learned: conventional DDPG with RIS; also DDPG and RPDRL without RIS, and own LyDDPG (p. 11-13).
metrics: Average transmit power consumption (W), cumulative reward, average delay (ms) versus episodes; power versus RIS elements, delay threshold, sensing SNR threshold, aerial users (p. 12-13).
complexity: none; only future work to reduce computational complexity (p. 13).
openness: none: no code or data link in the paper.
q1_support: p. 5: "When modeling these channels, we take into account the practical propagation characteristics under both far-field and near-field conditions". Missing: any 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data; the channel is a custom far-field/near-field line-of-sight model (p. 5-6).
q2_support: p. 12: "Fig. 7 compares the power consumption of RPDRL, LyDDPG, and the DDPG baseline under varying numbers of STAR-RIS elements". Missing: any statement that a trained model is tested in a scenario or configuration not used for training.
q3_support: p. 11: "Random Method (Benchmark 1): The phase-shift matrix of the STAR-RIS and the active beamforming at the ISAC GBS are randomly selected"; "DDPG with RIS (Benchmark 2): A conventional DDPG algorithm is employed"; p. 13: "the proposed RPDRL algorithm consistently achieves the lowest power consumption across the entire range"
q4_support: p. 13: "Future research directions include developing lightweight and scalable algorithms to reduce computational complexity". Missing: any FLOPs, parameter count, order of complexity or runtime of LyDDPG or RPDRL.
q5_support: p. 11: "The simulation parameters are set as follows: the bandwidth is set to B = 10MHz". Missing: any code or data link or DOI; the results come from the authors' own simulation.
notes: Area 5 (beamforming in an ISAC system); area 6 was considered because of the aerial users but not used, since the BS and the STAR-RIS are terrestrial and the aerial users are sensing targets (p. 4); area 3 loses to area 5 by the order of specificity. The learned decisions (beams and phase shifts) are physical layer; the Lyapunov delay term only shapes the reward, so above_phy does not apply. In q3 the learned baseline is the conventional DDPG; the benchmarks without RIS are variants of the proposed method and were not counted. The text does not state M, the STAR-RIS size of the main runs, the carrier frequency, the network architecture or the learning rates. Pages count the 15 pages of the file.
